reference.title: Reverse Hyper on Flat Bench
reference.listing: Page could not be read here (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice.

breathing.pattern: Exhale as the legs rise; inhale as they lower.

prescription.tempo: 1.2 s up, 0.6 s squeeze, 1.6 s down
prescription.progression: Pause at the top, then ankle weights

cues.text: Lie face down on a flat bench with the hips at the end and the legs hanging toward the floor, toes resting on it. Hold the bench.
Squeeze the glutes and lift both legs, straightening them, until they are level with the body.
Pause with the legs level; do not crank the low back into an arch.
Lower with control back to the floor.

mistakes.mistake: Swinging the legs up with momentum
mistakes.fix: Lift and lower under control; pause at the top.

mistakes.mistake: Over-arching the low back at the top
mistakes.fix: Stop when the legs are level with the body.
Hold the bench and keep the trunk down.
Straighten the legs as they rise.

kinematics.norm: From flexed (legs hanging) to about level with the body or slightly past (clinical opinion)
Bent with the toes on the floor at the bottom, straight at the top (clinical opinion)
Controlled, with a pause at the top (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #2958, Reverse Hyper on Flat Bench, video (movement reference; page not readable here)
Macadam and Feser 2019, gluteus maximus EMG excitation during dynamic body-weight hip extension: a systematic review (Int J Sports Phys Ther 14(1):14-31; PMC6350668)
Callaghan, Gunning and McGill 1998, the relationship between lumbar spine load and muscle activity during extensor exercises (Phys Ther 78(1):8-18)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Raise the legs only to level: arching past it loads the lumbar spine.
Make sure the bench is stable and cannot tip.
regressions: Prone hip extension on the floor (one leg).

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Gluteus maximus extends the hips to raise the legs from hanging to level; prone hip extension drills draw moderate to high gluteus maximus activity (Macadam and Feser 2019).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Gluteus maximus extends the hips to raise the legs from hanging to level; prone hip extension drills draw moderate to high gluteus maximus activity (Macadam and Feser 2019).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension with the knees straight (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension with the knees straight (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: The lumbar extensors work as the legs reach level and just above (Callaghan 1998 on prone leg-extension tasks).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: The lumbar extensors work as the legs reach level and just above (Callaghan 1998 on prone leg-extension tasks).
muscleNotes.core: Keep the trunk still on the bench and stop the low back over-arching at the top (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Pull the chest onto the bench so the trunk stays put (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_l: Pull the chest onto the bench so the trunk stays put (clinical opinion).
